content:
anna: Noticing a sudden rise in small-range GETs during the new safetensors bundle swap. Disk IO climbs and latency tails increase.

billy: Can confirm. Pattern looks like lots of clients doing full-shard fetches after a failed checksum/manifest race.

carol: Idea: split the initial response into tiny 'compact-header' payload and defer full header+payload parsing. Compact header contains bundle_id, shard_id, chunk_count, and a content-hash stamp. Clients can decide whether to request full slices or wait for a lease.

dmitri: I like that. Server-side we can also maintain a small token bucket per-bundle and hand out prefetch slots. If bucket empty, return 409 with Retry-After or a small backoff window header. That prevents everyone falling back to full blob pulls.

billy: How about a 'prefetch-lottery' response when under pressure? Response 202 with X-Prefetch-ETA: 120ms;prefetch-slot=0. Client can either poll or join a short-poll websocket for notification.

anna: Keep it simple first: add X-Compact-Header boolean and a /weights/header endpoint that returns compact JSON so clients can cheaply inspect. Example: ```http
GET /weights/header?bundle=abc&shard=3
200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "bundle": "abc",
  "shard": 3,
  "chunks": 12,
  "format": "safetensors",
  "hash": "sha256:..."
}
```

carol: Client flow suggestion: 1) HEAD/header probe 2) if lease allowed -> request lease (POST /weights/lease) 3) server grants lease_id with max_chunks 4) client streams chunk ranges. If lease denied, client uses range-chunk fallback but with aggressive coalescing to the shared cache.

dmitri: Edge case: mixed-format bundles need lease scope at bundle-level, not shard-level; leases must be transferable across worker restarts if we want resilience. Use a lightweight lease store (etcd/redis) with short TTL and allow lease renewal.

billy: On the perf note: parsing safetensors metadata on the server costs ~2-4ms per shard but when multiplied by 10k concurrent probes it hurts. Instead, persist compact headers in the index store at bundle creation time. That converts parse cost to a single write at publish time.

anna: We also need client heuristics to avoid stampeding on cold nodes: prefer local cache + peer cache hinting. Add header X-Cache-Hint: peer://node-id when server can suggest a nearby peer that already holds it.

carol: Security: leases should be scoped to API key and PV (project) so one customer can't hog another's slots. Also include an audit id in lease responses for tracing.

dmitri: Failure modes: if a client takes a lease and OOMs mid-warmup, we should allow quick revocation and expedite the next candidate. Lease revocation API: DELETE /weights/lease/{lease_id} with reason code.

buildbot: buildbot: pushed header-endpoint + lease-stub to canary @ 1769001200. Logs: /deploys/weights/header-canary.

billy: For the RFC follow-up, we should define: 1) compact-header schema 2) lease semantics + TTL/renewal rules 3) error codes and backoff guidance 4) client recommended fallback flow (HEAD -> header -> lease -> range-chunk).

anna: Action items: @carol to draft compact-header schema; @dmitri to prototype lease store + revocation; @billy to write client fallback examples + small SDK helper; I'll run a stress test against canary and post results.

carol: Will include example HTTP snippets and a small state-machine diagram in the RFC.

anna: Cool, meet-back in two days after initial results.
